items.title: Major tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to fears of AI slowdown
items.summary: Hundreds of billions of dollars in market value has been wiped from major tech firms in a stock market rout after the US midterm elections sparked concerns of a slowdown in AI development Following Democratic wins after election campaigns run on slowing AI, shares in firms across the tech and artificial intelligence sectors plummeted The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite stock index closed down by more than 5.5% to lose an estimated $2.5tn in market capitalisation, according to Dow Jones data, while other key US stock indexes also saw big losses in their worst days since 2025 The sell-off comes on top of broader concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off Democrats in races across the US campaigned to slow the onslaught of data centres and AI, and there were dozens of measures on ballots around the country aimed at restricting the development of the hubs crucial for powering the technology Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector Shares in companies heavily exposed to AI…

items.title: Mozambique: Finland donates €1M food from Ukraine to Cabo Delgado displaced
items.summary: The Government of Finland on Wednesday donated food to support 330,000 people affected by the armed conflict in the Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado. The initiative, valued at around €1 million, involved the purchase of food products from Ukraine The donation, comprising rice and soya oil, was formally handed over on Wednesday in Pemba, Cabo Delgado, by Finland’s Ambassador to Mozambique, Satu Lassila, to the Cabo Delgado provincial government and the World Food Programme (WFP) On the occasion, the Finnish ambassador expressed concern about the humanitarian situation in the province, which has been affected by attacks by extremist groups for almost a decade “The humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado is worrying. items.title: Delhi's toxic winter air is back - is the Indian capital prepared for pollution?
items.summary: People exercise in a park in Delhi on Thursday, breathing in hazy, polluted air There are two cardboard boxes in Meenu Rana's living room in Delhi. One is filled with Diwali decorations and twinkling lights. The other holds air purifiers "The mornings have already started feeling stuffy. It will get worse in the coming days, so it's better to be prepared," says the 43-year-old teacher She is not alone. Every year, as winter and the festive season approach, residents of India's capital begin preparing for something far less celebratory: months of breathing polluted air Delhi and its satellite cities record some of the world's highest pollution levels through the year. But as winter sets in, the air often becomes unbearable Falling temperatures and slower winds trap pollutants close to the ground instead of allowing them to disperse.

items.title: Government to mobilize about 27 billion meticais for mitigation of El Niño
items.summary: Maputo, 05 Nov (AIM) – The Mozambican government plans to mobilize approximately 27 billion meticais (1.7 billion US dollars at the current exchange rate) to implement the 2026/27 National Plan for Mitigating the Impacts of El Niño weather phenomenon. The plan aims to cover sectors of agriculture, health, education, water supply, food assistance, and social protection sectors. According to the Prime Minister Benvinda Levi, who was speaking on Wednesday at the country’s parliament, Assembly of the Republic, in response to concerns raised by parliamentary groups, the measure is also aimed at distributing agricultural input kits to over 185,000 households, incusing the construction of multi-purpose silos to complement small-scale irrigation systems, and the rehabilitation or construction of dams, water supply systems, and multi-purpose boreholes, “all aimed at benefiting more than one million people.” The 2026/27 rainy season points to normal rainfall in the Northern provinces of Nampula, Cabo Delgado, and Niassa.

items.title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening
items.summary: Cetirizine is commonly used to relieve allergy symptoms Kenyan pharmacists have warned women against inserting allergy tablets into their vaginas in an attempt to make them tighter, following the spread of potentially dangerous medical advice on social media The warning follows a wave of social media posts promoting cetirizine - a widely available oral antihistamine used to treat allergies - as a way of tightening the vagina, supposedly to enhance sexual pleasure Although antihistamines can sometimes cause dryness as a side effect, experts say this does not strengthen vaginal muscles "Dryness is not tightness... instead, it may increase friction, discomfort, and the risk of tissue injury," the Pharmaceutical Society of Kenya (PSK) said "Inserting oral tablets is unsafe. Cetirizine tablets are made to be swallowed.
